items.title: Tony Marino interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 25, 2025
items.q: Mike Formanek speaking of my peers.

ctx.x: Did you have a short list of bass players that you said, “I want to sound like that”?
Well I would put Scott LaFaro up there, I’d put Charlie Haden up there, I’d put Dave Holland. Oh there’s so many. Paul Chambers I was really into, Ron Carter, oh there’s a © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-

lot. There’s a lot of great young players. I love the Swedish bass player Anders Jormin – he’s a newer guy now. Mike Formanek speaking of my peers. Steve Respina. Steve Gilmore was a big influence on me because he was part of Phil Woods’ group, also Bill Goodwin. Bill Goodwin – I hooked up with him and we had a guitar trio with our late great friend Vic Juris that was the first record I did was through Bill. That was a really great hook-up for me.

items.title: Tony Marino interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 25, 2025
items.q: I did it once in the Water Gap with Michael Formanek that both of us played.

ctx.x: Yeah he did “Coltrane’s Meditation” it was every five years he would do it. And I got to do a few of them. I got to do them in Europe and I got to play double bass with Reggie Workman for instance. The one we recorded was with Cecil McBee. I did it once in the Water Gap with Michael Formanek that both of us played. So there were a few episodes of that he would do you know, and his wife Caris wrote/transcribed the melodies and so we had that form to pull out. I remember when we played with – it was Reggie Workman,…
Rubbing elbows with those gentlemen from the earlier era is so enriching.
